solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: something flipped over is turned end to end, so the word is read from the back

parts.note: tops are lids, as on jars

explanation.surface: An instruction to watch someone's eyelids roll back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lids' tempts toward eyes, but here they are the tops of containers.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to notice or catch sight of it, a plain synonym for seeing.

indicators.note: 'ran out' suggests things scattered or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A heap of confectionery has been used up.
explanation.definitionFit: Praline is a confection of nuts and caramelised sugar, so it is a kind of sweet.

indicators.note: 'after Tuesday' tells us the abbreviation for the weekday goes first, with the other pieces following it

parts.note: TU is the short form of Tuesday
a do is a party
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone is planning a house party for the day after Tuesday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' here is a royal dynasty, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were an English royal dynasty, and a ruling family is called a house, as in the House of Windsor.

clue.text: Computer file maybe not working, boy saves nothing

parts.note: a system that is down is not working

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it safe inside, so one piece holds another

parts.note: a lad is a boy
O, the figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A computer is broken, and a boy is not saving any of his work.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'maybe' signals that a computer file is just one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A download is data transferred to your machine from a network, typically a computer file.

clue.text: Deafening, irritating noise, first of all?

definitions.text: Deafening, irritating noise, first of all?

indicators.note: 'first of all' asks for the opening letter of every word before it

parts.note: the initial letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a loud, annoying noise is what to notice first.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both defines and builds the answer: the three initials make the loud noise described.
explanation.definitionFit: A din is a loud, unpleasant, prolonged noise, exactly the racket described.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: enclosed in paper, as a present is

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the idiom for bringing something to a close; the second is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something completed is said to be concluded or brought to an end, and a present is covered in paper before giving.

clue.text: Country where I live in shabby lair

indicators.note: 'in' places the pieces before it inside the rearranged word
something shabby is run-down and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
taken as written
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: Someone names the country where they live in a run-down den.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberia is a country on the west coast of Africa, an example of a nation.

clue.text: A figure lost in Bikini, say

parts.note: taken as written
a toll is the number of lives lost, as in a death toll

explanation.surface: Someone has lost their figure while wearing a bikini.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bikini' is not the swimsuit but Bikini Atoll in the Pacific, the site of nuclear tests; the 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Bikini is a ring-shaped coral reef in the Marshall Islands, an example of an atoll.

indicators.note: wild suggests something out of control, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener is told to dig near an untamed bush.
explanation.definitionFit: The gardenia is an evergreen shrub grown for its fragrant white flowers.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a spar along the bottom of a sail
second meaning: to thrive or grow rapidly

explanation.surface: A Polish person sets out to make money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' at the start of the clue hides its lower-case sense of a spar.
explanation.definitionFit: On a sailing boat the boom is the horizontal spar for the sail, and a business that booms flourishes.

clue.text: Train line going the wrong way — one's not to be trusted

indicators.note: travelling the wrong way means moving backwards, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: a rail is the track a train runs on

explanation.surface: A train is heading in the wrong direction, so the railway can't be relied on.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who tells untruths cannot be believed, which is what a liar is.

indicators.note: as an adjective suspect means dubious or unsound, so the letters are not to be trusted in this order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A poor, thin suspect has been let out of custody on terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' reads as a noun, the person released, but it is the adjective signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner freed early on condition of good behaviour is said to be out on parole.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: precisely right, an idiom
second meaning: where glasses sit on the face

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the idiom for spot on; the second is literal, where glasses perch.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means precisely accurate, and glasses literally rest on the bridge of that facial feature.

clue.text: Relic oddly missed in dry capital city

indicators.note: 'in' places the kept letters inside the word that follows

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne

indicators.note: missing the odd-numbered letters leaves only the second, fourth and so on

parts.note: the even letters, second and fourth

explanation.surface: A relic has gone missing in a dry capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: BRUT is the wine term for very dry, as on a champagne label.
explanation.definitionFit: Beirut is the capital city of Lebanon.

clue.text: Arch of colours from artist in front of ship

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
taken as written
the bow is the front of a ship

explanation.surface: A painter stands at a ship's prow and sees a coloured arc.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainbow is the arc of spectrum colours seen in the sky after rain.

clue.text: Good heavens, I don't come cheap!

parts.note: dear means expensive
I, spoken of as an object, is me

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise followed by someone boasting that they are expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, 'I don't come cheap' says the speaker is expensive: 'me' is 'dear'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise or dismay, interchangeable interjections.

indicators.note: something difficult is awkward or troubled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist goes through hard times.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a French painter, a leader of the Fauvist movement.

parts.note: a strike is industrial action by workers
time is up when it is finished

explanation.surface: Something begins once a workers' walkout has ended.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike up a conversation or tune is to begin it.

clue.text: Lighter part of Merlot or Chablis

indicators.note: 'part of' says the letters are a portion of the words that follow

parts.note: runs across the end of the first word, the middle word and the start of the last

explanation.surface: Part of a wine selection is lighter, as in less heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lighter' reads as a comparative about the wines, but it is a noun: something that gives light.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch is a portable light source, something that lights up, so a lighter.

indicators.note: 'Some' asks for only a portion of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A question about a tub kept in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the hidden letters spell the domestic tub described.
explanation.definitionFit: A bath is the large tub in a home's bathroom used for washing.

parts.note: a bin is where rubbish goes
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: An instruction to put out the rubbish and get out of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' is not a building but an old name for the numbers game, also called housey-housey.
explanation.definitionFit: Bingo was long known in Britain as house or housey-housey, and 'House!' is the winner's shout.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a larva, which looks like a worm
second meaning: informal word for things to eat

explanation.surface: Worms as a meal, the way a bird sees them.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect larva is soft and wormlike, and in slang the same word means eats or a meal.

indicators.note: changed says the letters are altered into a different order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A performer has swapped smart clothes for tatters.
explanation.definitionFit: An organist is a musician who plays the organ, often in church.

indicators.note: refusing something means turning it away, so that piece is left out

parts.note: a gain is a benefit
taken as written, the letter removed

explanation.surface: Someone gains by saying no to an alcoholic drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Gin is a spirit flavoured with juniper, an example of an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Who needs mince to cook Chinese dish?

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
more letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A question asking who has to cook minced meat for a Chinese meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chow mein is a Chinese dish of stir-fried noodles with meat or vegetables.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in cricket, a set of six balls bowled

explanation.surface: Six parcels have been delivered and the round is complete.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bowler's deliveries come in sets of six called an over; 'deliveries' suggests post, not balls.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket over is six balls from one bowler, and something over is ended or done.
